ext_staking.onchain_row_bunker: Lido bunker mode: exits are slower than usual
ext_staking.guide_onchain_intro: Some pools delegate your coins on the network itself. They work differently from the fixed-rate pools this guide describes, and each pool page says which kind it is.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_rate_body: You receive what the network paid, minus the commission stated on the pool page. The pool shows what it observed over the last 30 days; that is history, not a forecast, and it can be zero.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_lock_lead: No lock and no early exit.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_lock_body: You can ask to exit at any time, and the exit then waits for the network's unbonding period. The wait is an estimate and the request cannot be cancelled.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_coins_move_body: A stake takes the coins from your own deposit address on this platform to a staking wallet this platform holds, and delegates them from there. They come back to your address when an exit is released.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_shares_body: Your position is a share of the pool. Rewards raise the value of every share; a validator penalty on the network lowers it for every holder, including you.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_disclosure_body: Every on-chain pool page is generated from the pool's records and versioned. A stake is placed against the version you read, with five acknowledgements this platform keeps on file.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_what_to_expect: What to expect after you stake
ext_staking.guide_onchain_rewards: None of the above applies to an on-chain pool. There is no distribution schedule and no auto-compound setting: the network pays whatever it pays, the platform observes it on chain each epoch, and it raises the value of every holder's shares as it arrives. There is nothing to claim, because the rewards are not a balance this platform is holding for you — they are already yours, inside the pool, and they come back as coins when you unstake. To take only the rewards out, unstake the part of your position they represent; the rest keeps earning.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_risks: In an on-chain pool the reward is whatever the network pays, and it can be zero. A validator penalty on the network reduces the pool's value for every holder. An exit waits for the network's unbonding period, which is an estimate, and cannot be cancelled once requested. While staked, your coins are held in a wallet this platform controls and are not insured.

ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_exit_requested_desc: from the moment you ask to leave.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_unbonding_desc: with the date the coins are expected back.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_returned_desc: once they are in your address.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_failed_desc: if the stake could not be placed. It is refunded, with the reason.

support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.stops.0.bod: I'll show you how to narrow this down to the items you actually want. Nothing is spent while we look — a purchase is only made when you confirm it on the item's own page.
support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.stops.1.bod: Type here to match an item, a collection or a creator. The results underneath re-run as you type, so there's nothing to press.
support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.stops.2.bod: This opens category, collection, sort order and a minimum and maximum price. Setting a maximum price is the quickest way to stop seeing items you don't want to spend that much on.
support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.stops.3.bod: These split the results by how the item is sold. "Buy now" is a set price you pay once; an auction means you place a bid, someone else can outbid you, and it closes at a fixed time whether or not you're watching.
support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.stops.4.bod: Each card shows the current price and the currency it's priced in — an auction shows the leading bid, not a price you can just pay. Opening a card takes you to the item, where you'll see the full cost including network fees before you confirm anything.
support_assistant.guides.browse_the_nft_market.title: How to find and buy an NFT
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.0.b: Futures here are leveraged, so both your gains and your losses are multiplied, and a move against you can close the position and take the margin you put up. This walkthrough shows you how to read this list before you commit anything.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.1.b: Type a coin here to narrow the list to the contracts on it. Only what appears on this page can be traded as futures — holding a coin in your wallet does not mean there is a contract for it.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.2.b: This narrows the list to markets that allow 100x or more, which is the number shown against every row. The higher it goes the smaller the move that wipes out your margin — around 1% against you at 100x — so read it as how much room you have to be wrong, not as how much you can win.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.2.t: What the leverage number costs you
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.3.b: The list is ordered by maximum leverage, highest first, so the contracts that liquidate the fastest sit at the top by default. Switch this to Name to browse alphabetically instead.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.3.t: Why the top of the list is not the best of it
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.stops.4.b: Each row is a perpetual contract, and picking one opens the trading terminal, where you set your own leverage, size and stop. Nothing is ordered from this page, and the leverage shown here is the ceiling that market allows, not a setting you have to use.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_futures_market.title: Choosing a futures market
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.stops.0.bod: Staking sets a token aside for a fixed length of time and pays a rate while it is set aside. This page lists every pool that is open right now, and these few steps are how you narrow it down to one that fits you.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.stops.1.bod: These shortcuts re-filter the whole list in one click. Short lock brings the pools that tie your funds up for the least time to the front, and High APR the ones paying the most.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.stops.2.bod: Open this to limit the list to one token, or to a rate range. You can only stake a token you already hold, so setting the token here saves you opening pools you cannot use.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.stops.3.bod: One pool can offer several lock lengths, so this shows the shortest and the longest it accepts — and longer terms are usually the ones paying the higher rate. Your funds stay locked for whichever length you choose, and ending a stake before that date costs a fee, so pick a length you can go without the money for.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.stops.4.bod: Open a pool to choose your exact term and amount and see the estimated reward first. Nothing leaves your balance until you confirm on that screen.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_staking_pool.title: How to pick a staking pool
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.0.b: Copying means this trader's trades are placed in your account, with your money — their losing trades land in your balance the same way their winning ones do. I'll show you what to look at before you pick someone.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.1.b: This narrows the list to traders running at a risk level you are willing to sit through. A high-risk trader takes larger and faster positions with your funds, so both the gains and the losses arrive bigger.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.1.t: How hard your balance can swing
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.2.b: This ranks traders by one figure from their past — return, win rate, or how many people already follow them. It describes trades that are already finished, so a trader at the top of this list can still lose money on the next one.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.3.b: Each card is one trader and the record they have published: past return, win rate, and how many people copy them. Those numbers are history, not a forecast — nothing here promises what your own account will do.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.stops.4.b: Open a trader to read their full record and their terms: the share of your profits they take, and the smallest amount you can start with. You choose how much of your balance to allocate on their page, and you can pause or stop copying at any time.
support_assistant.guides.choose_a_trader_to_copy.title: How to pick a trader to copy
support_assistant.guides.complete_verification.stops.0.bod: This is where identity verification happens. It gates some features, so it is worth doing carefully once rather than three times.
support_assistant.guides.complete_verification.stops.1.bod: Levels are cumulative and each one opens more of the platform. Start with the lowest one that covers what you actually need.
support_assistant.guides.complete_verification.stops.2.bod: If something was rejected, the reason is shown here. Read it before resubmitting — the same document will be rejected the same way.
support_assistant.guides.complete_verification.stops.3.bod: Photograph all four corners, in daylight, with no flash on the plastic. Blur and glare are the two reasons most submissions come back.
support_assistant.guides.complete_verification.title: How to get verified
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.0.body: Everything that has moved in or out of your account is on this page. Let me show you how to narrow it down.
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.0.title: Finding a transaction
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.1.body: Deposits, withdrawals, transfers and trades are all listed here together. Use the filter and search above the table to narrow to one kind — that is usually the fastest way to find what you're after.
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.1.title: Everything, filtered
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.2.body: The status column is what answers 'where is my money'. Pending means it is still on its way and no action is needed; completed means it has arrived and your balance already reflects it. Opening a row shows the timestamps and the reference — if you need to ask us about it, quote that reference.
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.stops.2.title: Reading the status
support_assistant.guides.find_a_transaction.title: How to find a transaction
Here you trade with another user rather than with the platform. The crypto is held in escrow from the moment a trade opens until both sides confirm, so neither of you is ever holding the other's funds unprotected.
This switches between a short list of people picked to fit what you asked for and the full board of live offers. The picks are the top of that same board, so nothing is being kept from you.
This sets which way the trade goes. If you sell, your own crypto is locked into escrow as soon as a trade opens, and you cannot spend it again until you confirm the payment reached you.
Set the asset, how much you want to trade, and how you want to pay. Your amount is checked against each offer's own minimum and maximum, so anyone who cannot handle that size drops out of the list.

Each row is a person who sets their own price, limits and payment methods, so it is worth comparing a few rather than taking the first. Opening one starts a real trade and moves the crypto into escrow.
support_assistant.guides.find_someone_to_trade_with.title: How to find someone to trade with
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.0.body: I'll walk you through it, from picking a plan to confirming it. Nothing leaves your wallet until you press the last button.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.0.title: Putting money into a plan
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.1.body: The large percentage applies to the whole term, not per year, and the chip beside it says whether the plan settles as a gain or as a deduction — read that before the number. Underneath are the smallest and largest amounts it takes and the currency it is in; open a plan to go on.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.1.title: What a plan is offering
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.2.body: Opening a plan takes you to its own page, where you set the amount. That amount leaves your wallet the moment you confirm and stays committed until the term ends — the plan's minimum and maximum are shown under the box, and the wallet it comes from is named at the bottom of the panel. If that wallet is short, the request is refused.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.2.title: How much you're committing
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.3.body: On that same page you pick a term. It sets the date your money comes back, not how much comes back — on one plan, a longer term pays the same amount later. Choose the date you are comfortable being without the money.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.3.title: What the term actually changes
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.4.body: The confirm button on that page moves the money immediately. If you change your mind before the term ends you can cancel, but a cancellation returns your original amount only and gives up the outcome, whichever way it was going.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.4.title: Confirming it
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.5.body: Everything you have open lives on Portfolio, with the time left on each one. Open a position there to see how it settled, or to cancel it while it is still running.
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.stops.5.title: Where to watch it
support_assistant.guides.invest_in_a_plan.title: How investing works here
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.0.body: I'll walk you through picking an offering and putting money into one. Nothing leaves your balance until the last step, so you can follow along and stop wherever you like.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.0.title: Joining a token sale
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.1.body: Only the ones under Active are taking money right now. Upcoming sales have not opened yet and Completed ones are closed — you can read their terms, but there is nothing to buy.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.1.title: Which sales you can join
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.2.body: This opens the full terms — how much has been raised, the smallest amount you can put in, and the price of the phase running now. That price is set per phase and changes when the sale moves to the next one, so the figure on this card is only the current one.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.2.title: Opening an offering
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.3.body: Opening a sale takes you to its own page, where you type an amount or drag the slider. The tokens you would receive and the platform fee are worked out as you type — the fee is added on top, so the total taken from your balance is more than the number you enter.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.3.title: How much you're putting in
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.4.body: That page also asks for a receiving address, and it has to be one on the project's own chain. Check it character by character — a distribution sent to the wrong address cannot be pulled back, by us or by anyone else.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.4.title: Where the tokens will be sent
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.5.body: Confirming there takes the amount and the fee out of your balance straight away; the tokens arrive later, on the schedule the project published. A sale can miss its goal, and a token can end up worth less than you paid for it, so only commit money you can do without.
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.stops.5.title: Committing the money
support_assistant.guides.join_a_token_sale.title: How to join a token sale

support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.0.body: I'll walk you through it. Three choices, and each one narrows the next — nothing is charged while we do this.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.0.title: Adding funds
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.1.body: Start here. This decides which of your wallets the money arrives in, and it changes what you can pick further down.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.1.title: Where the funds should land
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.2.body: This is what will be sitting in your balance afterwards. Only the currencies that wallet supports are offered.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.2.reveal: Pick a wallet type in the step above and the currency list opens here.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.2.title: Choose the currency
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.3.body: Each method has its own limits and arrival time, and some are only available in certain countries — the ones you can actually use are the ones shown. Choosing one takes you to the payment step.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.3.reveal: Choose a currency above and the payment methods you can use appear here.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.3.title: Pick how you're paying
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.4.body: What you see after this depends on the method. Card and bank methods ask for an amount and hand you to the payment provider; a crypto deposit gives you an address to send to instead. Either way, nothing has been charged yet.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.stops.4.title: What happens next
support_assistant.guides.make_a_deposit.title: How to add funds
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.0.body: This page reveals itself one step at a time — each choice decides what you are asked next. I'll point at each step as it appears, so answer them as we go rather than skipping ahead. Take your time on the destination: that is the one thing nobody can undo for you afterwards.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.0.title: Taking money out
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.1.body: Start here. Your money is held in separate wallets, and this decides which one the withdrawal is taken from — only the wallets holding something are offered.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.1.title: Which balance it comes from
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.2.body: This is what leaves your balance, and it narrows the ways you can be paid. The amount available in each is shown beside it.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.2.reveal: Pick a wallet type in the step above and the currency list appears here.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.2.title: Choose the currency
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.3.body: Pick how you want to receive the funds. What you're asked for next depends on this — the fee and the arrival time are shown against each one.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.3.reveal: Choose a currency above and the methods that can pay it out appear here.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.3.title: Where it's going
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.4.body: Check this character by character before you go on. A withdrawal sent to the wrong address cannot be reversed by us or by anyone else — this is the single most important field on the page.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.4.reveal: Pick a method above and the details form opens, with this field in it.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.4.title: The destination
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.5.body: The fee and the amount that will actually arrive are shown beneath as you type. Your available balance excludes anything currently held in open orders.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.5.reveal: This sits in the same form as the destination, which opens once you have picked a method.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.5.title: How much
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.6.body: You may be asked for a confirmation code. After that it goes into the queue — you can follow it on your transaction history.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.6.reveal: The button sits at the bottom of the details form, once an amount and a destination are filled in.
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.stops.6.title: Submit the request
support_assistant.guides.make_a_withdrawal.title: How to withdraw
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.0.body: You can always have a person instead of me. Here is how, and what to include so the first reply is a useful one.
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.0.title: Reaching the team
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.1.body: This starts a new conversation with the team. Everything you and they say stays on one thread.
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.1.title: Opening a ticket
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.2.body: Anything already open is here with its status. Replying on the existing thread gets a faster answer than opening a second one about the same thing.
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.stops.2.title: Your existing tickets
support_assistant.guides.open_a_ticket.title: How to reach a person
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.0.body: This screen is where you set a bot up and watch what it does afterwards. Nothing on it places a trade until you build a bot and start it yourself.
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.0.title: Your bots, in one place
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.1.body: Each of these is a different rule for when to buy and sell — buying a fixed amount at intervals, laddering orders around a price, or reacting to an indicator. Picking one opens the builder with that strategy already chosen.
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.1.title: Pick how it decides
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.2.body: Here you choose the market, the rules and how much of your balance the bot is allowed to spend. A live bot trades real money out of your wallet and can lose it, so keep that allocation to an amount you are willing to see fall.
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.2.title: Building the bot
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.3.body: Paper mode runs the same strategy against real prices using simulated funds, so you can watch how it behaves before any of your own money is exposed. The figures in this panel are a test result — they are not earnings and cannot be withdrawn.
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.3.title: Try it without money first
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.4.body: Once a bot is started it appears here with its state and its profit or loss so far, and this is where you pause or stop it. Stopping ends the strategy, but anything the bot has already bought stays in your wallet until you sell it.
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.stops.4.title: Watching it, and stopping it
support_assistant.guides.run_a_trading_bot.title: How trading bots work here
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.0.body: Two-factor authentication is the single biggest thing you can do here. It takes about a minute.
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.0.title: Securing your account
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.1.body: Everything to do with signing in lives here — your password, and the second factor.
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.1.title: The security section
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.2.body: You will scan a code with an authenticator app and then enter the six digits it shows. Save the backup codes somewhere that is not your phone.
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.stops.2.title: Turning it on
support_assistant.guides.secure_my_account.title: How to turn on two-factor
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.0.body: Everything the store sells is listed on this page. You narrow the list down to what you want, add it to your cart, and pay from there.
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.0.title: The catalogue
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.1.body: Typing here trims the list to products whose name or short description contains what you typed. Clearing the box brings the whole catalogue back.
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.1.title: Search by name
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.2.body: This opens the category list, a maximum price, and an in-stock-only switch. The badge counts how many filters are currently trimming your results, so if the page looks emptier than you expect, that is where to look.
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.2.title: Pick a category or cap the price
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.3.body: This changes the order of the same results — cheapest first, newest, or best rated. Nothing is removed from the list, so use it to compare rather than to narrow.
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.3.title: Reorder what you see
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.4.body: Anything you add collects here, and checkout starts from this button. Payment is taken from your platform wallet in the item's own currency, so the order will not go through if that wallet does not hold enough.
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.stops.4.title: Your cart, and paying
support_assistant.guides.shop_and_checkout.title: How to buy from the store
support_assistant.guides.understand_my_wallets.stops.0.bod: Money here lives in separate wallets rather than one pot. That trips up almost everybody the first time, so let me show you.
support_assistant.guides.understand_my_wallets.stops.1.bod: Each type funds a different part of the platform. A balance sitting in the wrong one is the usual reason a page says you have nothing to trade with.
support_assistant.guides.understand_my_wallets.stops.2.bod: Available is what you can spend right now. Anything in an open order or a pending withdrawal is held and shows separately — it has not gone anywhere.
support_assistant.guides.understand_my_wallets.stops.3.bod: Transfers between your own wallets are instant and free. This is what you want when the money is there but the page you need says it is not.
support_assistant.guides.understand_my_wallets.title: How your wallets work
support_assistant.guides.understand_referral_rewards.stops: Everything you earn here starts with one link. I'll show you where it is, who counts as a referral, and what actually pays.
This is the only link that credits a sign-up to you — the button on the right copies it. Somebody who registers without going through it cannot be attributed to you afterwards.
Posts the same link to a social account, an email, a text message or a QR code. The link inside every one of them is identical, so it makes no difference which you pick.

A sign-up stays pending until that person does the thing the programme pays for. Only active referrals earn you anything, and that is usually why somebody has referrals here and nothing in earnings yet.

Everyone who used your link shows up here with the state they are in, and View all opens the full list. If a person tells you they signed up through your link and they are not on this list, their registration was not attributed to you.
These are the actions that earn you a reward and what each one is worth; View details shows every rate in full. Nothing outside this list pays — a sign-up on its own may earn you nothing at all.
support_assistant.guides.understand_referral_rewards.title: How the referral programme works
support_assistant.operations.cancel_pending_kyc.descriptio: We will withdraw the verification submission you have waiting for review. It is recorded as a rejection, so you will not be able to submit for that level again for 24 hours. Anything you have already been approved for is unaffected, and your uploaded documents are not deleted.
support_assistant.operations.cancel_pending_kyc.label: Withdraw my verification submission
support_assistant.operations.mark_notifications_read.descr: We will mark every unread notification on your account as read. Nothing is deleted — they all stay in your notifications list, and you can mark any of them unread again.
support_assistant.operations.mark_notifications_read.label: Mark my notifications as read
support_assistant.operations.resend_verification_email.des: We will send the verification link again to the email address on your account.
support_assistant.workflows.catch_up_on_notifications.step: We will mark every unread notification on your account as read. Nothing is deleted — they all stay in your notifications list, and you can mark any of them unread again.
They are all still here, now without the unread markers. Anything you want to come back to can be marked unread again from this page.
That is the backlog cleared. Nothing was removed.
support_assistant.workflows.find_missing_money.steps.escal: If it is genuinely not in your history and not in any wallet, that needs a person. Open a ticket here and include the reference from your history — that is the thing they will look it up by.
Someone will pick that up and reply on the ticket.
support_assistant.workflows.find_missing_money.steps.histo: Almost every missing payment is either still pending or landed somewhere unexpected. Let's look at your history first — I'll show you how to narrow it down and read the status.
If it is there and pending, it is on its way. If it is there and completed, the next step will show you where it went.
support_assistant.workflows.find_missing_money.steps.walle: A completed payment that you cannot see is usually in a different wallet from the one you are looking at. This is where to check.
If it is in neither place, the last step opens a ticket with the team.
support_assistant.workflows.find_missing_money.title: Track down a payment you cannot find
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.confirm.de: Once you have paid, your deposit appears here with a status. Pending means it is still on its way; completed means the balance already reflects it.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.confirm.do: If it is not here after the arrival time your payment method quoted, tell me and I will bring in a person.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.deposit.de: Now I'll walk you through the deposit form itself — which method to pick, the currency, and the amount. Nothing is submitted until you press the button yourself.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.deposit.do: That is the whole form. Once you have paid, the last step is checking it arrived.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.wallets.de: First I'll show you how balances are held here — money sits in separate wallets rather than one pot, and that is what confuses almost everybody on the first deposit.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.steps.wallets.do: Now you know where a balance lands. Next, the deposit form itself.
support_assistant.workflows.first_deposit.title: Add funds for the first time
Withdrawals are usually gated on identity verification, so we start there. If you are already verified this takes a moment and we move on.
Next, where the money you can withdraw actually lives.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.steps.wallets: Now the balance itself. Only what is available can be withdrawn — anything in an open order or an earlier pending withdrawal is held, and that is the usual reason the amount you expect is not the amount offered.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.steps.withdra: Last, the withdrawal form. I will stop on the destination field, because that is the one thing nobody can undo for you afterwards.
That is everything. Your request will appear in your transaction history with a status.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.title: Take money out for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.offers: Everything currently raising, with what each one is selling and how far along it is. Read the terms — a token sale is not a deposit, and the value can go to zero.
Anything you buy into shows up on your transactions page.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.transa: Your purchases and, where the sale has a release schedule, when each portion becomes available.
That is the whole picture. Release schedules are set by the project, not by us.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.verify: Token sales are usually gated on identity verification. We start there because it is the most common reason somebody cannot take part.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.title: Take part in a token sale
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.brow: Everything available, with its price and whether it is in stock. Add what you want to your basket as you go.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.cart: Check the quantities and the total before you go on. Orders are paid from your wallet balance, so make sure the right wallet has enough in it.
Checkout is the next step from here.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.orde: Every order you have placed, with its status and any tracking. This is the page to check before asking where something is.
If an order is stuck, quote its number and I will bring in a person.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.title: Buy something from the store
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.steps.resend.de: We will send the verification link again to the email address on your account.
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.steps.sign_in.d: Once you have opened the link in that email, sign in here. If the email has not arrived after a few minutes, check the spam folder before trying again.
You are on the sign-in page. If the link still has not arrived, tell me and I will bring in a person.
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.title: Get back into your account
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.steps.resubm: Your submission has been withdrawn. Because a withdrawal is recorded as a rejection, the next submission for that level opens in 24 hours — go to the verification page to check where you stand and get the right documents ready.
You are on the verification page. It shows your current status, and you can submit again once the 24 hours are up.
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.steps.withdr: We will withdraw the verification submission you have waiting for review. It is recorded as a rejection, so you will not be able to submit for that level again for 24 hours. Anything you have already been approved for is unaffected, and your uploaded documents are not deleted.
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.title: Start your verification again
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.steps.notifi: Every sign-in, withdrawal and security change is recorded here. Read back through it — anything you do not recognise is worth telling us about straight away.
If you see something you did not do, tell me now and I will bring in a person immediately.
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.steps.two_fa: The single biggest thing you can do is two-factor authentication. I'll show you exactly where it is and what to expect.
Now let's make sure you can see anything that happens on the account.
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.title: Lock down your account
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.steps.fun: When you move off practice mode, this is the balance a real trade draws on and where to top it up.
That is everything. Practise first — there is no cost to it.
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.steps.ter: This is the walkthrough the binary screen ships with. It covers the chart, the expiry, and the practice mode — start in practice mode.
Next, where the money for a real trade comes from.
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.title: Get started with binary options
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.steps.brows: Traders you can follow, with their history. Past performance is not a promise — allocate only what you would be willing to lose on somebody else's decisions.
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.steps.subsc: Everyone you currently follow and how much is allocated to each. Pausing and stopping both live here — this is the page you want if you have changed your mind.
Stopping does not close positions that are already open. Check those separately.
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.title: Follow another trader
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.steps.in: Everything you have running and what it has returned. Results here are not guaranteed by us, whatever a plan's headline rate says.
That is where to check on it from now on.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.steps.pl: Managed plans, each with its minimum, its term and its stated return. This is money managed on your behalf, which is a different thing from trading it yourself.
Next, where an investment is tracked.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.title: Invest in a managed forex plan
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.steps.fund: A position needs a funded balance. Let's confirm yours first — it is the usual reason a first order is refused.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.steps.term: Now the forex screen itself — this is the walkthrough it ships with, covering the chart, the order ticket and your open positions.
That is the terminal. Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains — start small.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.title: Get started on the forex terminal
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.fund.des: A plan is funded from your wallet, so let's confirm what is available first.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.plans.de: Each plan states its rate, its term and its currency. The term is a commitment — read what happens if you want out early before you commit anything.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.plans.do: Anything you start appears in your portfolio.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.portfoli: Everything you have running, what it has returned so far, and when each one matures.
That is where to check on it from now on.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.title: Put money into an investment plan
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.market: These are live offers from other people. Check the trader's completed-trade count and their terms before you commit — you are trading with a person, not with us.
Once you open a trade, funds are held in escrow until both sides are done.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.paymen: Before your first trade you need at least one payment method saved, so the person on the other side knows how to pay you or how to be paid. Add one here.
With a method saved, you can be matched. Next, the market.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.trades: Every trade you open lives here with its stage and its countdown. This is the page to be on while a trade is running — it is also where the dispute button is if something goes wrong.
Never release funds until you have confirmed payment arrived in your own account, not just that the other side says it has.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.title: Buy or sell peer-to-peer for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.start_referring.steps.programm: This is your referral link and what the programme pays. The link is the only thing that attributes a signup to you — a referral who signs up without it cannot be credited afterwards.
What each referral has earned you and whether it has been paid out yet. A reward usually has conditions attached — the referred person completing something, not merely signing up.
If a referral is missing here, that is worth a ticket — include when they signed up.
support_assistant.workflows.start_referring.title: Start earning from referrals
An order needs a funded balance in the right wallet, and that is the usual reason a first order is refused. Let's check yours before anything else.
support_assistant.workflows.start_spot_trading.steps.termi: Now the terminal itself. This is the walkthrough the trading screen ships with — the chart, the order book, and the order ticket.
That is the terminal. Nothing is placed until you press the button yourself.
support_assistant.workflows.start_spot_trading.title: Place your first trade
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.fund.descr: Staking locks tokens you already hold, so let's start with what is in your wallets and which of it is actually available.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.fund.label: Check what I hold
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.pools.desc: Each pool has its own rate and its own lock period. The lock is the part to read carefully — your tokens are committed for that long, and leaving early may cost you.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.pools.done: Once you have staked, your position appears on the next page.
Your stakes, what they have earned, and when each lock ends. Rewards are claimed from here.
That is the whole cycle: stake, earn, claim when the lock ends.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.title: Stake for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.confirm.d: A completed swap appears in your history like any other movement. This is where to confirm what you received.
If a swap is missing here after the network has confirmed it, tell me.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.swap.desc: This is the walkthrough the swap screen ships with. It covers picking the two tokens, slippage, and the network fee — which is charged by the network, not by us.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.swap.done: Next, where to check the swap actually landed.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.title: Swap one token for another
